# m.options.open_interest

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The open interest of each US-listed options contract at the end of each trading day.

Call it from a session `m`, made with `dm.MassiveSession()`:

```python
m.options.open_interest(symbols=None, *, root=None, contract_type=None, start=None, end=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None, on_error=None)
```

- [Methods](README.md#query-methods): `fetch()`, `poll(interval)`
- Read from: REST
- `poll()` by default: `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`, which holds only the latest poll's rows, one row per `Symbol` and `Date`

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Arguments

A linked argument follows its rule under [shared arguments](README.md#shared-arguments) on the dataset index.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`symbols`](README.md#symbols) | Option contracts; leave it out for every contract. |
| `root` | An OCC root, such as `"SPXW"`, or several; leave it out for every root. |
| `contract_type` | `dm.ContractType.CALL` or `PUT`; leave it out for both. |
| [`start`](README.md#start) | The first trading day. |
| [`end`](README.md#end) | The last trading day. |
| [`sort`](README.md#sort) | Any of Massive's field names, such as `"open_interest"`. Fields: any REST field under [Massive fields](#massive-fields). |
| [`order`](README.md#order) | The direction of `sort`. |
| [`limit`](README.md#limit) | The most rows to return, in total. A watchlist's `fetch()` caps every request instead. |
| [`filters`](README.md#filters) | Further endpoint parameters, such as `{"expiration_date": "2026-12-18"}`. Keys: `expiration_date`, `expiration_date_gt`, `expiration_date_gte`, `expiration_date_lt`, `expiration_date_lte`, `ticker_gt`, `ticker_gte`, `ticker_lt`, `ticker_lte`. |
| [`on_error`](README.md#on_error) | What a bad symbol or row does in this call (`dm.ErrorPolicy`). None, the default, takes each cause from the session's `MassiveConfig.on_error`. |

## Plans

How recent the data is on each of Massive's plans, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Open Interest by Contract (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Options Basic | Not included |
| Options Starter | Not included |
| Options Developer | Not included |
| Options Advanced | End-of-day, All history |
| Options Business | Not included |
| Historical Options Analytics Business | End-of-day, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The row's instrument, as Massive's ticker. From REST `ticker`: "The options ticker symbol (e.g., O:SPY260123C00687000)." |
| `OptionRoot` | String | The OCC root symbol of the contract (e.g., SPXW). Differs from the underlying for weekly roots and for contracts adjusted after a corporate action (e.g., AMCR1). |
| `ContractType` | String | The contract type. Possible values: call, put. |
| `Date` | String | The trading date the open interest applies to (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `ExpirationDate` | String | The date the contract expires (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `OpenInterest` | long | The number of outstanding contracts that have not been closed or exercised, as of the last open interest update of the day. |
| `StrikePrice` | double | The strike price of the contract. |
| `UnderlyingTicker` | String | The ticker of the contract's underlying (e.g., SPX). Weekly and adjusted roots are folded in, so SPXW contracts report SPX and AMCR1 contracts report AMCR; see root to tell them apart. Massive's `root` is the `OptionRoot` column. Massive sends an index without its `I:` prefix (`SPX`). So this column won't match `Underlying` in `m.options.chain()`, `m.options.snapshots()`, or `m.options.contracts()`, which write `I:SPX`. |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, by the local clock. Rows that arrive together share it. It isn't Massive's time, and later rows can carry earlier times. In a `poll()` table, it's the time of the poll the row's values came from. |
